  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study reports quantitative measures of agreement between an in vitro human GI microtissue model and human clinical outcomes for drug-induced diarrhea, including predictive accuracy (84%) and sensitivity (79%). It compares the predictive performance of the microtissue assay to Caco-2 cells and discusses translation from preclinical animal studies.",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "The study focuses on gastrointestinal toxicities (GITs) and drug-induced diarrhea as adverse events, which falls under toxicology.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "oncology",
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study mentions oncology drugs and their GI toxicities, and also discusses general drug safety testing applicable across therapeutic areas.",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "The study develops and validates a human 3D gastrointestinal microtissue model and compares its predictive performance to Caco-2 cells.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat",
    "dog",
    "non-human-primate"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study references preclinical data from rat and dog studies, and discusses non-human primate studies in the context of predicting clinical outcomes.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study uses both TEER (a measure of barrier function, secondary biomarker) and clinical diarrhea incidence (a hard outcome, primary-hard) to assess predictive accuracy."
